content: Electrical stimulation therapy is a treatment modality that involves the application of electrical currents to specific muscles or nerves in children diagnosed with cerebral palsy. This therapy aims to improve muscle strength, enhance motor function, and reduce spasticity by stimulating neuromuscular activity. It is often used as an adjunct to conventional physical therapy to optimize functional outcomes. The electrical impulses delivered during the therapy mimic the natural signals sent by the nervous system, thereby promoting muscle contraction and improving coordination. This approach may also help prevent muscle atrophy and improve circulation in affected areas. The therapy is typically tailored to the individual needs of the child, taking into account the severity of their condition, the specific muscles or motor functions targeted, and their overall treatment goals.
